name: Assaf Gordon
why_notable: Revived GNU time after 21 years without a release. Version 1.7 (1996) had been patched separately by every distribution, most famously for a bug that reported peak memory four times too high. His GNU Time 1.8 (November 2017) modernised the code with gnulib, absorbed the downstream patches, relicensed it under GPLv3+, and added -q and coreutils-style exit codes (125/126/127). GNU Time 1.9 (March 2018) fixed CPU-percentage reporting for runs under a second and is the version Linux distributions ship today. He is also the author of GNU datamash and has contributed to GNU coreutils.
